## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Dutiyadabba Sutta* (Ud 8.10; PTS Ud 93) is the tenth discourse of the eighth chapter of the *Udāna* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The core theme encapsulated in the discourse is that there is no destination that can be described for those who are rightly released from worldly existence [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into multiple modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels identified for the discourse include the *Sukhavarga* chapter of the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 30; including the *Udānavarga de Subaši*, UVS 30), corresponding Chinese versions in the *Faju yaosong jing* and related recensions (T 212.31, T 213.30), the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (Uv Kg 30), and a Vinaya narrative parallel in the Sanskrit Mūlasarvāstivāda *Cīvaravastu* (san-mu-kd7) [SuttaCentral]. The text is also explicitly mentioned in the *Mahāpajāpatigotamītherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 17) [SuttaCentral].

Computational text-reuse data from DharmaNexus corroborate these cross-linguistic parallels, showing strong alignments with the Sanskrit *Udānavarga de Subaši* (score 95, matching segment §4.1) and the Tibetan translation of the *Udānavarga* (D0326, score 75), as well as an alignment with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, the sutta shares extensive textual material with its immediately preceding companion discourse, the *Paṭhamadabba Sutta* (Ud 8.9, sharing 973 characters across segments §2.1_0–4.1), along with formulaic phrasing found widely across the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3, AN 5, AN 7, AN 8, AN 10) and *Majjhima Nikāya* (MN 2, MN 11, MN 16, MN 112, MN 131), and shared verse or prose material preserved in the commentary literature such as the *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā*, *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
